# the contributor audit: uniform cap envelopes and source-tie continuation

PASS after reading the complete uniform-finite-cap-envelopes-and-exact-source-tie-continuation-optimal-midpoint.md. The theorems are conditional analytic tools; their geometric hypotheses are not claimed at arbitrary bodies.

The uniform maximum displacement bound uses both the common exterior gap and the time-Lipschitz bound. The constant 4B/c follows by comparing the maximizing value with the trial value at the original mark. Substitution into the Taylor remainder gives exactly A s omega(A s), A=1+4B/c. Balanced gradients cancel mark displacement only after this O(s) localization.

The all-source Dini bound retains every maximizer at the time in question, a compact complement gap, and every covariance/chart derivative. The Dini comparison proof is valid: subtracting a small positive linear function from an alleged increase yields a minimum attained before the right endpoint and contradicts its strictly negative upper right derivative. Source entry must be handled anew and is not inferred from a prior menu.

A full positive circuit of d+1 gradients gives the printed invertible equal-cap Jacobian. Positivity persists and supplies a strict local maximum; the assumed global gap identifies its envelope globally. The distinction from a merely positive-spanning set is necessary and correctly retained.

Full-rank exact neutral constraints are correctly excluded at a stationary unrestricted minimum: they would permit simultaneous negative derivatives. On the regular k-1 source-tie manifold, stationary multipliers cancel curve acceleration. The reduced Hessian is exactly the same-menu weighted sum of profile Hessians. Negative value yields an actual decreasing tie curve. Zero first derivative, or zero reduced second derivative, alone does not produce a neutral path. No arithmetic conclusion or finite termination follows from these analytic tools.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
